A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, figures, tables, algorithms, and Appendices A–D. Additions, relocations, and figure renumbering can be identified without material evidence gaps.

before.justification: V1 reports original language-model experiments on SlimPajama and OpenWebText2, toy-model simulations, and CIFAR-10 sharpness experiments in Sections 3–5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds checkpoint-interpolation results and refinement-parameter sensitivity results in Figure 3 and Appendix C.1.

M1.justification: The SF and refined SF-AdamW procedures are unchanged, including the decoupling rule c_t = (1−β)C/t and its warmup-aware, capped implementation in Algorithms 1–2. Additional experiments and explanations do not introduce another method component.

E1.justification: Both versions use SlimPajama and OpenWebText2 language modeling, CIFAR-10, and the same toy objective. The interpolation analysis and C sweeps operate within retained coverage; they introduce no new data domain or task.

E2.justification: Existing AdamW, SF-AdamW, learning-rate schedule, and EWA comparisons are retained. The added interpolation analysis reuses constant/linearly decayed AdamW and constant-LR SF-AdamW; the new sensitivity tables retain vanilla SF-AdamW as the baseline.

E3.justification: Figure 3 introduces loss evaluation along interpolations between 2B- and 2.5B-token checkpoints. Appendix C.1 adds C-sweep evaluations on 9M held-out tokens across momentum values and two batch sizes. The retained experiments' training budgets and approximately 1.6M-token validation protocol remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a checkpoint-interpolation diagnostic of river tracking and explicit C-sensitivity results across momentum settings and batch sizes (Figure 3, Tables 5–6). These targeted additions extend the existing geometry and robustness analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed or repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new sensitivity tables continue to report point estimates.

E6.justification: V2 adds interpolation-loss profiles and test-perplexity entries. Table 5 reports 25.12 for vanilla SF at β1=0.95 versus 23.60 at C=100; Table 6 reports 26.09 for vanilla at β1=0.98 versus 23.88 at C=1000. These are newly reported test results; matched earlier plots and their results are retained.

T1.justification: Propositions 4.1–4.2, Lemma D.1, the SF reformulation, central-flow derivations, and averaging-weight approximation in Appendix D remain mathematically unchanged. Formatting and figure-reference updates do not alter the theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: river tracking without decay or auxiliary averaging, an EoS/central-flow explanation, and improved momentum robustness and large-batch performance through refinement.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new interpolation profiles as evidence of valley crossing versus floor tracking and argues that refined SF works without careful C tuning. Section 5 also clarifies how large β reduces recent-gradient influence. Existing small-model and theoretical-approximation limitations are retained.

D1.justification: V2 documents the interpolation endpoints and the sensitivity experiments' C/momentum configurations, fixed LR=2e-3 and β2=0.99, and 9M-token test evaluation. Existing implementation, code/data access, hardware, and training-time disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and overall positioning relative to WSD, weight averaging, SF, and EoS remain unchanged. The fuller Ahn et al. (2025) ICML entry is bibliographic; the interpolation discussion elaborates the existing connection to Wen et al. (2025).

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering are retained. V2 adds Appendix C.1 and an Impact Statement, makes localized explanatory and grammatical edits, and updates an affiliation and funding acknowledgment.

P2.justification: The document switches throughout to NeurIPS formatting, changing typography, text and figure widths, title treatment, running headers, and display placement. V2 adds Figure 3 and Tables 5–6, renumbers subsequent figures, and places both final averaging-weight grids together on one page.

improvement.justification: Figure 3 strengthens the geometric evidence for river tracking, while Tables 5–6 document tuning behavior beyond v1's selected configurations. These are useful, limited gains within existing small-model settings. Table 6 includes worse-than-vanilla choices, so the broad robustness interpretation still needs qualification.
